dn33:3.3.6: When a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places, seeing danger in the slightest fault, keeping the rules they’ve undertaken—
dn33:3.3.9: When a mendicant is very learned … penetrating them theoretically—
dn33:3.3.12: When a mendicant has good friends, companions, and associates—
dn33:3.3.15: When a mendicant is easy to admonish … taking instruction respectfully—
dn33:3.3.18: When a mendicant, in the diverse duties for their spiritual companions … is able to organize the work—
dn33:3.3.21: When a mendicant loves the teachings … being full of joy in the teaching and training—
dn33:3.3.24: When a mendicant is content with any kind of … supplies for the sick—
dn33:3.3.27: When a mendicant lives with energy roused up … not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities—
dn33:3.3.30: When a mendicant is mindful … able to remember and recall—
dn33:3.3.33: When a mendicant is wise … leading to the complete ending of suffering—
